source.creator: Lewis Carroll / John Tenniel
source.basis: Tenniel's Alice as coloured for The Nursery Alice (1890): yellow dress with blue trim, long fair hair with a band; the 'DRINK ME' bottle and 'EAT ME' cake (ch. 1) and her neck 'opening out like the largest telescope' (ch. 2).
source.notice: Based on Lewis Carroll's Alice's Adventures in Wonderland (1865), illustrated by John Tenniel — public domain.

source.creator: Lewis Carroll / John Tenniel
source.basis: Chapter 1, 'Down the Rabbit-Hole': Alice falls slowly past cupboards, book-shelves, maps and a jar of ORANGE MARMALADE; Alice drawn after Tenniel/Nursery Alice colouring (yellow dress, blue trim).
source.notice: Based on Lewis Carroll's Alice's Adventures in Wonderland (1865), illustrated by John Tenniel — public domain.

source.creator: Lewis Carroll / John Tenniel
source.basis: Chapter 6, 'Pig and Pepper': the Cat 'vanished quite slowly, beginning with the end of the tail, and ending with the grin'; drawn as Tenniel's grey tabby on a branch (not a striped pink/purple cat).
source.notice: Based on Lewis Carroll's Alice's Adventures in Wonderland (1865), illustrated by John Tenniel — public domain.

source.creator: Lewis Carroll / John Tenniel
source.basis: Chapter 1: the White Rabbit 'with pink eyes' takes a watch out of its waistcoat-pocket ('Oh dear! I shall be too late!') and hurries off; waistcoat and coat after Tenniel.
source.notice: Based on Lewis Carroll's Alice's Adventures in Wonderland (1865), illustrated by John Tenniel — public domain.

source.creator: Lewis Carroll / John Tenniel
source.basis: Chapter 7, 'A Mad Tea-Party', after Tenniel: the Hatter's tall hat with its price card ('In this style 10/6', ch. 11), spotted bow tie and teacup; not the Disney green-hat design.
source.notice: Based on Lewis Carroll's Alice's Adventures in Wonderland (1865), illustrated by John Tenniel — public domain.

source.creator: Beatrix Potter
source.basis: Potter's own text and watercolours: Peter's 'blue jacket with brass buttons' and his raid on Mr. McGregor's garden ('then he ate some radishes'). Original pixel design.
source.notice: Based on Beatrix Potter's The Tale of Peter Rabbit (1902) — public domain.

source.creator: Carlo Collodi / Enrico Mazzanti
source.basis: Mazzanti's 1883 illustrations: tall pointed cap ('a little cap of bread dough'), suit of flowered paper, bark shoes; chapter 17, where his nose grows with each lie and woodpeckers peck it back to size. No Tyrolean hat, bow tie or red shorts.
source.notice: Based on Carlo Collodi's The Adventures of Pinocchio (1883), illustrated by Enrico Mazzanti — public domain.

sprites.title: Pooh Bear and the Honey Jar

source.creator: A. A. Milne
source.basis: Milne's 1926 text (ch. V, 'In Which Piglet Meets a Heffalump': Pooh gets his head stuck in a honey jar). Original plain golden teddy-bear design — not based on E. H. Shepard's drawings, and no red shirt or other Disney elements.
source.notice: Based on A. A. Milne's Winnie-the-Pooh (1926) — public domain in the United States. Original bear design, not derived from E. H. Shepard's illustrations or Disney.

source.creator: Traditional; pictured by John Tenniel in Through the Looking-Glass (1871)
source.basis: Traditional rhyme ('Humpty Dumpty sat on a wall, Humpty Dumpty had a great fall'), first printed 1797; egg-man with a cravat sitting on a narrow wall after Tenniel's Looking-Glass illustration.
source.notice: Based on the traditional nursery rhyme Humpty Dumpty and John Tenniel's illustration for Through the Looking-Glass (1871) — public domain.

source.creator: Anonymous (St. Nicholas Magazine)
source.basis: The 1875 St. Nicholas Magazine tale: the cookie boy leaps from the oven and runs off, taunting his pursuers ('You can't catch me!'). Original design: iced eyes and smile, gumdrop buttons.
source.notice: Based on the folk tale The Gingerbread Boy (St. Nicholas Magazine, 1875) — public domain.

source.creator: L. Frank Baum / W. W. Denslow
source.basis: Denslow's Dorothy: blue-and-white gingham frock, plaits tied with ribbons, the Witch of the East's SILVER shoes (not ruby slippers); ch. 23-24, 'knock the heels together three times'; Toto as a small black dog.
source.notice: Based on L. Frank Baum's The Wonderful Wizard of Oz (1900), illustrated by W. W. Denslow — public domain.

source.creator: L. Frank Baum / W. W. Denslow
source.basis: Ch. 3: the Scarecrow stuck on a pole in a cornfield, his painted eye 'slowly wink[ing]' at Dorothy, crows unafraid of him; Denslow's blue Munchkin hat and suit stuffed with straw (not the MGM costume).
source.notice: Based on L. Frank Baum's The Wonderful Wizard of Oz (1900), illustrated by W. W. Denslow — public domain.

source.creator: L. Frank Baum / W. W. Denslow
source.basis: Ch. 5: the Tin Woodman rusted stiff with his axe raised until Dorothy oils his joints with the oil-can; he longs for a heart (given by Oz, ch. 16). Denslow's funnel-hatted tin man.
source.notice: Based on L. Frank Baum's The Wonderful Wizard of Oz (1900), illustrated by W. W. Denslow — public domain.

source.creator: L. Frank Baum / W. W. Denslow
source.basis: Ch. 6: the Lion bounds out with a terrible roar, is slapped on the nose for snapping at Toto, and cowers, wiping a tear — 'I'm a coward'. Denslow's shaggy-maned lion; no hair-bow or medal (MGM).
source.notice: Based on L. Frank Baum's The Wonderful Wizard of Oz (1900), illustrated by W. W. Denslow — public domain.

sprites.title: Huff, Puff and Blow the House In

source.work: The Story of the Three Little Pigs
source.creator: Joseph Jacobs (English Fairy Tales) / John D. Batten
source.basis: Jacobs' 1890 telling: 'Then I'll huff, and I'll puff, and I'll blow your house in' — the wolf blows down the house of straw. Plain natural wolf and pig; no 1933 Disney costumes (no sailor suits or hats).
source.notice: Based on the folk tale The Three Little Pigs as told in Joseph Jacobs' English Fairy Tales (1890) — public domain.

source.work: The Frog King, or Iron Henry (Kinder- und Hausmärchen no. 1)
source.creator: Brothers Grimm
source.basis: Grimms' tale of the crowned frog who becomes 'a king's son with kind and beautiful eyes'. The kiss follows the popular later retellings (in Grimm the spell breaks when the princess throws the frog at the wall). Original design.
source.notice: Based on the Brothers Grimm's The Frog King (1812) — public domain.

source.creator: Hans Christian Andersen
source.basis: Andersen's tale: the scorned grey duckling looks into the water and sees he has become a beautiful white swan. Original design.
source.notice: Based on Hans Christian Andersen's The Ugly Duckling (1843) — public domain.

source.work: The Hare and the Tortoise (Aesop's Fables)
source.creator: Aesop (traditional), tr. George Fyler Townsend
source.basis: Aesop's fable as in Townsend's 1867 translation: the Hare naps mid-race and the Tortoise plods past to win — 'slow but steady wins the race'. Original design.
source.notice: Based on Aesop's fable The Hare and the Tortoise (trans. G. F. Townsend, 1867) — public domain.

sprites.title: Puss in Boots Takes a Bow

source.work: Le Maître chat ou le Chat botté (Puss in Boots)
source.creator: Charles Perrault / Gustave Doré
source.basis: Perrault's tale and Doré's 1862 engravings: a grey tabby cavalier in tall cuffed boots and a broad plumed hat, sweeping a courtly bow. No sword, mask or Spanish 'Zorro' styling (avoids the DreamWorks character).
source.notice: Based on Charles Perrault's Puss in Boots (1697) and Gustave Doré's illustrations (1862) — public domain.

source.creator: Joseph Jacobs (English Fairy Tales) / John D. Batten
source.basis: Jacobs' 1890 telling: the magic beans grow overnight into a beanstalk 'up till it reached the sky', and Jack climbs to the giant's castle above the clouds. Original design.
source.notice: Based on the folk tale Jack and the Beanstalk as told in Joseph Jacobs' English Fairy Tales (1890) — public domain.

source.work: A Study in Scarlet / The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
source.creator: Arthur Conan Doyle / Sidney Paget
source.basis: Holmes on the trail with 'a large round magnifying glass' examining footprints (A Study in Scarlet, 1887); deerstalker cap, Inverness cape and straight pipe after Sidney Paget's Strand illustrations (from 'The Boscombe Valley Mystery', 1891). No actor likeness.
source.notice: Based on Arthur Conan Doyle's Sherlock Holmes stories (1887–1892), illustrated by Sidney Paget — public domain.

source.creator: Traditional ballads; Walter Scott / Howard Pyle (1883)
source.basis: The outlaw archer in Lincoln green from the ballads and Howard Pyle's The Merry Adventures of Robin Hood (1883); splitting the rival's arrow in the bullseye comes from Locksley's shot in Scott's Ivanhoe (1819). Plain hood, no film costume.
source.notice: Based on the Robin Hood legend, Walter Scott's Ivanhoe (1819) and Howard Pyle's The Merry Adventures of Robin Hood (1883) — public domain.

source.work: A Visit from St. Nicholas; Thomas Nast's Santa Claus
source.creator: Clement Clarke Moore (attrib.) / Thomas Nast
source.basis: Moore's poem ('laying his finger aside of his nose, and giving a nod, up the chimney he rose'; a belly 'like a bowlful of jelly') and Thomas Nast's Harper's Weekly Santa (1863–1886): fur-trimmed suit, white beard, sack of toys. Not the Sundblom/Coca-Cola advertising art.
source.notice: Based on A Visit from St. Nicholas (1823) and Thomas Nast's Santa Claus illustrations (1863–1886) — public domain.

source.creator: Traditional; Krampus greeting cards (c. 1890–1910)
source.basis: Alpine St. Nicholas-eve folklore as on turn-of-the-century 'Gruss vom Krampus' cards: shaggy horned devil with a long red tongue, rattling chains and a bundle of birch switches. Original design.
source.notice: Based on the traditional Alpine Krampus figure of folklore — public domain.
